steps.message:
This is a breaking change to a published contract, so I'm stopping before touching it.

`routes/users.js:6` is the `GET /users` response shape. Renaming `userId` → `user_id` there changes the field every client reads. `README.md:3-5` names the consumers — the web app, iOS 3.2+, and the nightly partner export — and states that field names are part of the contract and that changes go through a versioned endpoint. Shipped iOS builds can't be updated in lockstep, so an in-place rename breaks them until users upgrade.

The rename itself is one line; the question is how to land it.

questions.question: How should the userId -> user_id rename land on GET /users?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId in the existing response. Non-breaking: new clients read user_id, old clients keep working. Requires a later cleanup commit to drop userId once consumers migrate.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README's stated process: add a v2 (or equivalent) users route with snake_case, leave the current route untouched. Largest change, but it is what the repo documents.

options.label: Rename in place anyway
options.description: Change line 6 to user_id and nothing else, exactly as asked. Breaks the web app, shipped iOS 3.2+ builds, and the nightly partner export until each is updated.
